newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Basis down, demand slow.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Basis down, demand slow.

text.p: Falling domestic and export demand pressured most soybean meal basis offers in U.S. cash markets Wednesday, brokers said.
"We're a dead market," one Tennessee-based dealer said. "Things are very slow and demand is pretty slack."
There was also additional talk in the markets that China will cancel some of the large soymeal purchases it made in December, traders said. But no direct evidence has surfaced in U.S. cash markets.
"I've heard the rumors, but physically, I haven't seen any of it being cancelled," one export trader said.
This week there have been only a few cars of soymeal traded as domestic buyers secure a little inventory before the Christmas holiday, traders said.
"You can't feed an animal air," said one dealer.

The huge premium that December CBOT soymeal holds to January was still discouraging buyers to do much spot business, dealers said. Late Tuesday morning, December soymeal futures were trading at $230.00 a ton while January was trading at $221.50.
